title: Nonlinear stationary axisymmetric tidal response of Kerr black holes
statement: Determine the nonlinear stationary axisymmetric tidal response of four-dimensional Kerr black holes across multipoles, including matching to a worldline effective field theory. Recover established quadrupolar results and identify the response coefficients accessible within axisymmetry.
source_locator: Rodríguez et al., section 6.3.2, PDF p.112; Gounis et al., section 5.1; Chakraborty et al., introduction and final discussion.
status_basis: The review explicitly identifies the incomplete multipolar calculation and EFT matching. The October 2026 Kerr-Newman result concerns linear response. A targeted later-literature search found no closure of this specific gap.
plain_summary: How does a spinning black hole respond beyond first order to a steady surrounding gravitational tide? A complete treatment must connect the spacetime solution with well-defined response coefficients.
assumptions: Four-dimensional vacuum general relativity, with a regular Kerr event horizon and stationary axisymmetric external gravitational tides.
Specify the applied tidal moments, normalization and matching prescription; distinguish nonlinear tidal order from order in black-hole spin.
Separate conservative static response from dissipation and frequency-dependent response.
State the spin range explicitly. For subextremal calculations use |a|<M in geometrized units; an extremal limit requires its own boundary analysis.
scope: The literature gap is multipolar nonlinear response and EFT matching, not the already-studied linear Kerr response.
target: A controlled response calculation or theorem with explicit multipole coverage and identifiable coefficients.
success_criteria: State which tidal orders, multipoles and spin values are covered.
Show that horizon-regular solutions satisfy the field equations and match the declared EFT.
Recover established limits and state which coefficients cannot be determined under axisymmetry.
known_results: Gounis et al. calculate an axisymmetric quadrupolar tidal tail and make a broader vanishing claim; the later review still identifies incomplete multipolar matching.
The October Kerr-Newman preprint reports a linear conservative Love matrix, leaving beyond-linear response separate.
prerequisites: General-relativistic perturbation theory and horizon boundary conditions.
Multipole expansions, worldline EFT and symbolic tensor calculation.
significance: Response coefficients connect compact-object structure with inspiral modeling. The value of a bounded result depends on its new coverage and interpretation, not merely on another zero coefficient.

requirements.experiment: None for a conditional GR calculation; observational tests require additional evidence.
requirements.data: Published equations and conventions; no observational dataset is required.
requirements.compute: A finite-order symbolic calculation may start locally, but expression growth can dominate memory. No runtime or budget has been measured.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Vacuum GR, specified tidal environment and horizon regularity; only response combinations identifiable in the chosen symmetry sector.

obstacles: Gauge-dependent tails can be mistaken for physical response.
Axisymmetry may conceal independent EFT operators.
All-orders language can exceed the calculation actually established.

steps: Check source definitions and retained perturbative orders.
Substitute derived fields into the equations and inspect horizon and axis regularity.
Audit source-response separation and EFT matching independently.
Compare the nonrotating and quadrupolar limits with the cited results.

validation.statement_alignment: A finite-order calculation establishes only its stated channels and approximation; it is not a complete all-multipole or observational result.
